changed.title: The 4 by 4 bipartite graph with mask 55 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 4 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 4 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 4 => (55 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: A witness prices the gate saving from negation on mask 55. Compare its shared and negated wires with the checked AND/OR minimum for the same graph.
changed.sketch: Encode the 16 promised input pairs as wire truth tables. Start with the 4 row masks and 4 column masks. For each of at most 4 gates choose earlier wires and AND, OR or NOT. Order binary operands to remove duplicates. Match every output bit to mask 55. Among circuits of this size at least one NOT is needed by the checked AND/OR floor. Return a gate list and replay all 16 output bits.

changed.title: Exact field-linear scan dimension for counting distinct affine-code words that satisfy local truth tables
changed.statement:
∀ (F : Type) [Field F] (k m t d : ℕ),
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  ∀ (base : W) (gen : Fin m → W) (scope : Fin t → Finset (Fin k)),
    (∀ v : Fin k, ∃ j : Fin t, v ∈ scope j) →
    let key := fun a : Fin m → ZMod 2 => base + ∑ h : Fin m, a h • gen h
    let rk := fun S : Finset (Fin k) =>
      let M : Matrix (Fin m) S (ZMod 2) := fun row coord => gen row coord.val
      M.rank
    let need := (Finset.range (t+1)).sup (fun i =>
      let P := Finset.univ.filter (fun seen : Fin k => ∃ before : Fin t, before.val < i ∧ seen ∈ scope before)
      let Q := Finset.univ.filter (fun future : Fin k => ∃ after : Fin t, i ≤ after.val ∧ future ∈ scope after)
      2^(rk P + rk Q - rk Finset.univ))
    let T := fun idx : Fin t => (↥(scope idx) → ZMod 2) → Bool
    let count := fun tests : (j : Fin t) → T j =>
      Nat.card {w : W // w ∈ Set.range key ∧ ∀ j, tests j (fun tested => w tested.val) = true}
    (∃ (s : Fin d → F)
       (step : (j : Fin t) → T j → ((Fin d → F) →ₗ[F] (Fin d → F)))
       (out : (Fin d → F) →ₗ[F] F),
      ∀ tests : (j : Fin t) → T j,
        out ((List.finRange t).foldl (fun cur stage => step stage (tests stage) cur) s) =
          (count tests : F)) ↔ need ≤ d
changed.unlocks: Determines the exact linear memory for counting local tests restricted to a key code, including cuts with disjoint but correlated coordinate sets.
changed.context: Group legal prefixes by their sets of compatible suffixes. Each nonempty set is a coset of the future-only subcode. Equal or disjoint cosets give 2^(r(P)+r(Q)-r(all)) classes. Choose one word per class and pin its past and future projections by local singleton tables. The count matrix on these choices is an identity over every field and factors through the scan state. Conversely extend each class by feasible new coordinates, filter by the current table and add its prefix counts to the next classes. Initialize and finish with one class.

changed.title: Every Boolean square can be rematched into few groups with constant diagonal blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ), 0 < m → m^2*4^m ≤ n →
  ∀ G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool,
    ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (group : Fin n → Fin (2*(n/m))),
      ∀ (x y z w : Fin n), group x = group y → group x = group z → group x = group w →
        G x (π y) = G z (π w)
changed.unlocks: constructs a rematching and partition with few monochromatic diagonal squares
changed.context: While at least m4^m rows and columns remain, take 2m rows. For each in turn keep columns carrying its more frequent bit. At least m columns survive. At least m selected rows used the same bit, giving a constant m by m block. Pair its rows and columns and remove both sets. The blocks number at most floor(n/m), and fewer than m4^m≤floor(n/m) unpaired rows remain. Pair these as singleton groups. Complementary pairs of equal sizes extend the matching to all labels.

changed.title: Sharp support bound and equality cases for the Walsh spectrum of a triangular Boolean product circuit
changed.statement:
∀ t : ℕ,
  let V := Fin t → ZMod 2
  ∀ (A B : Fin t → Fin t → ZMod 2) (γ : V),
    let sources := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin t)).filter (fun j =>
      ∃ i, j < i ∧ (A i j ≠ 0 ∨ B i j ≠ 0))
    let c := fun (j : Fin t) (z : V × V) =>
      γ j + ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ioi j, (z.1 i * A i j + z.2 i * B i j)
    let live := (Finset.univ : Finset (V × V)).filter (fun z =>
      ∀ j, c j z ≠ 0 ∨ (z.1 j = 0 ∧ z.2 j = 0))
    let lhs := 2 * 4^sources.card * live.card
    let rhs := (4^sources.card + 1) * 4^t
    lhs ≤ rhs ∧
      (lhs = rhs ↔
        (∀ j, j ∉ sources → γ j = 1) ∧
        ∀ j ∈ sources, ∀ k ∈ sources, ∀ z, c j z = c k z)
changed.unlocks: determines the extremal support count and equality conditions for the triangular coefficient test at each number of feedback sources
changed.context: A source j kills a frequency when its later affine coefficient vanishes and its own pair is nonzero. The initial event has probability 1/2. Process sources downwards. The union U already killed depends only on later pairs, so its new measure is at least 3/8+Pr(U)/4. Equality at each update requires all later killed events to lie in the current zero hyperplane. Each such event spans its own hyperplane since the three nonzero local pairs span the two-bit affine plane. A zero sink coefficient kills 3/4. Allow 2 to 4 hours.

changed.title: Total matrix rank bounds the simultaneous nonsingularity set of finite-field linear pencils
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of grid points where all listed matrix perturbations are invertible by their total rank budget
changed.context: Multiply the determinants. The value at zero is one. In a basis ending in a basis of ker M_i the last columns are constant, so factor i costs degree at most rank M_i. At fixed degree, moving an exponent unit from a smaller positive exponent to a larger unsaturated one decreases that product. Fill a exponents then b. Allow 2 to 5 hours.

changed.title: A rank-one field-linear map can agree somewhere with every prescribed multiplier exactly when the reciprocals avoid zero in their affine span
changed.statement:
∀ (E K : Type) [Field E] [Field K] [Algebra E K] [FiniteDimensional E K]
    (S : Finset K), (0 : K) ∉ S →
  ((∃ C : K →ₗ[E] K, Module.finrank E (LinearMap.range C) ≤ 1 ∧
    ∀ z ∈ S, ∃ x : K, x ≠ 0 ∧ C x = z*x) ↔
    (0 : K) ∉ affineSpan E ((fun z : K => z⁻¹) '' (↑S : Set K)))
changed.unlocks: characterizes prescribed nonzero field multipliers that a single correction of rank at most one can meet
changed.context: For nonempty S write the nonzero rank-one map as C(x)=u f(x). The equation C(x)=zx for x nonzero implies f(u/z)=1 after cancelling f(x). Thus the reciprocal set lies on one affine hyperplane avoiding zero. Conversely if its affine span omits zero, a linear functional L takes value one there. Annihilate the direction space and normalize at a basepoint. Take C(x)=L(x) times the field unit and x=1/z. The empty set uses the zero map. Allow 1 to 3 hours.

changed.title: Cyclic runs count the input masks with nonzero Walsh coefficient and bound the loss under a singular three-tap mix
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (d : ℕ),
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let sign := fun (t : B) => if t = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else -1
  let mix := fun (s : ℕ) (x : V) (i : I) => x (i-(s : I)) + x i + x (i+(s : I))
  let nl := fun (y : V) (j : I) => y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2)
  let coeff := fun (s : ℕ) (a b : V) =>
    ∑ x : V, sign (dotProduct a x + dotProduct b (nl (mix s x)))
  let support := fun (s : ℕ) (b : V) => Finset.univ.filter (fun mask : V => coeff s mask b ≠ 0)
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  let h := if 3 ∣ k/g then 2*g else 0
  ∀ b : V,
    let edge := fun (w : V) (i : I) => b (i-2)*w (i-1) + b (i-1)*w (i+1)
    let run := fun (i : I) =>
      ((List.range k).takeWhile (fun offset => decide (b (i+(offset : I)) = 1))).length
    let r := if ∀ i : I, b i = 1 then k - Nat.gcd k 2 else
      ∑ i : I, if b i = 1 ∧ b (i-1) = 0 then 2*((run i + 1)/2) else 0
    (∃ base : V, ∀ a : V, a ∈ support d b ↔
      ∃ u : V, a = base + mix d (edge (mix d u))) ∧
    (support 0 b).card = 2^r ∧
    (support d b).card ≤ 2^r ∧ 2^r ≤ 2^(2*h) * (support d b).card
changed.unlocks: An affine basis enumerates the contributing predecessors of a requested output mask in the shared-key transfer. Summing the run weights prices a full layer.
changed.context: Polarize the mask polynomial. Its matrix after mixing is M E M, where E is the selected cycle adjacency in the term. On the radical, q(x)+q(0) is linear. Extend it to a frequency. The other extensions differ by the polar image, and the checked quadratic Walsh formula detects exactly these. A proper run gives a path on l+1 vertices: the endpoint forces alternate kernel entries zero, leaving one free only for odd order. The full cycle kernel is two-periodic. Each multiplication by M drops rank by at most its nullity h; on a spacing orbit its kernel repeats A,B,A+B.

changed.title: Local linear equations characterize all raw key shifts preserving any selected bits of both scheduled first-round words
changed.statement:
∀ (k : ℕ) [NeZero k],
  let I := ZMod k
  let B := ZMod 2
  let V := I → B
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : V) (i : I) => w (i-(s : I))
  let mix := fun (d : ℕ) (w : V) (i : I) => w (i-(d : I))+w i+w (i+(d : I))
  let out := fun (d u v : ℕ) (name c x : V) (j : I) =>
    let y := mix d (rot u x + name)
    y j + (1+y (j+1))*y (j+2) + rot v x j + c j
  let test := fun (d u v : ℕ) (z : V) (j : I) =>
    let a := mix d (rot u z)
    a j = rot v z j ∧ ((k = 1 ∨ k = 3) ∨ (a (j+1) = 0 ∧ a (j+2) = 0))
  ∀ (row col cr cc z : V) (S T : Finset I),
    (∀ x : V,
      (∀ j ∈ S, out 1 1 0 row cr (x+z) j = out 1 1 0 row cr x j) ∧
      (∀ i ∈ T, out 2 3 4 col cc (x+z) i = out 2 3 4 col cc x i)) ↔
    (∀ j ∈ S, test 1 1 0 z j) ∧ (∀ i ∈ T, test 2 3 4 z i)
changed.unlocks: Computes the exact period space of arbitrary requested first-round bits directly from the two tap stencils. It gives the raw key parity lower bound for overlapping windows.
changed.context: Write a for the mixed shift and y for the mixed word. The change at j has variable part a(j+2)y(j+1)+a(j+1)y(j+2). Each mixed coordinate is a nonzero form on the key. Adjacent forms are distinct unless all translates of the tap mask agree. At widths above three a nonzero mask of at most three sites cannot be constant. At width two the mix is the identity. Hence both coefficients must vanish, leaving a(j) equal to the reinjected shift. At widths one and three y is constant across sites, so the nonlinear product vanishes identically. Intersect the requested tests.

changed.title: Independent flips in symbol pairs bound simultaneous polynomial prediction on permutations of binary words
changed.statement:
∀ w : ℕ,
  let K := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin (w+1) → K
  let I := V × Fin (w+1)
  let s := 2^w
  ∀ (A : Finset V) (c : V → Finset I → K),
    let m := A.card
    let pred := fun (p : Equiv.Perm V) (a : V) =>
      ∑ S ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset I)).filter (fun S => S.card ≤ w),
        c a S * ∏ j ∈ S, p j.1 j.2
    let bad := (Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm V)).filter (fun p =>
      ∃ a ∈ A, pred p a ≠ ∏ i : Fin (w+1), p a i)
    let total := 2^s * Nat.choose (2*s) m
    let empty := ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (s+1), Nat.choose s j * Nat.choose (2*j) m
    Nat.factorial (2*s) * (total - empty) ≤ s * total * bad.card
changed.unlocks: A quantitative joint-error bound on arbitrary marked permutation blocks.
changed.context: Under a common prefix shift and independent last-bit pair flips, summing a predictor over shifts leaves a value independent of flips. Correctness on all shifts prescribes one flip per occupied prefix. For h occupied prefixes at most a 2^(-h) fraction of flip masks succeeds on all shifts. Average over the base permutation and count uniform marked subsets contained in random unions of pairs.

Average over the base permutation and count uniform marked subsets contained in random unions of pairs.

changed.title: The full one-round parity has a closed radical size and adaptive parity-query agreement at every cyclic width
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat) [NeZero k] (spacing : Nat),
  let K := ZMod 2
  let I := ZMod k
  let W := I → K
  let D := W →ₗ[K] K
  let s := Nat.gcd k (2*spacing)
  let loss := Nat.gcd k 2 + (if 3 ∣ k/s then 2*s else 0)
  let p := (k-loss)/2
  ∀ (start inject : I) (name c : W),
    let phase := fun x : W =>
      let z := fun i : I => x (i-start) + name i
      let y := fun i : I => z i + z (i+(spacing:I)) + z (i-(spacing:I))
      ∑ i : I, (y i + (1+y (i+1))*y (i+2) + x (i-inject) + c i)
    let rad := (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun v =>
      ∀ u : W, phase (u+v) + phase u + phase v + phase 0 = 0)
    rad.card = 2^loss ∧ (p = 0 ↔ k ≤ 2 ∨ ((k = 3 ∨ k = 6) ∧ ¬3 ∣ spacing)) ∧
    ∀ d : Nat,
      let run := fun (ask : Fin d → Nat → D) (x : W) =>
        (List.finRange d).foldl (fun h j => 2*h + (if ask j h x = 0 then 0 else 1)) 0
      let hits := fun (ask : Fin d → Nat → D) (rule : Nat → D) (bias : Nat → K) =>
        ((Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun x =>
          phase x = rule (run ask x) x + bias (run ask x))).card
      let cap := (2^k + 2^(k-(p-d)))/2
      (∀ ask rule bias, hits ask rule bias ≤ cap) ∧ ∃ ask rule bias, hits ask rule bias = cap
changed.unlocks: Agreement for the all-output parity even when the cyclic mix is singular.
changed.context: Let S shift sites and A=S+S^-1. The raw polar operator is A M_d squared, since the mix M_d and A commute and M_d is self-adjoint. Squaring gives M_(2d). This fixes every vector in ker A, which consists of words of period two. Thus its product kernel splits: x maps to M_(2d)x and x-M_(2d)x. On each of s spacing orbits the mix kernel repeats u,v,u+v, giving two free bits iff 3 divides k/s. For rank 2p a codimension-h leaf loses at most 2h in rank. Walsh bounds each leaf; asking one factor in each normal-form product attains.

Walsh bounds each leaf; asking one factor in each normal-form product attains.

changed.title: An erroneous pooled decoder on uniform copies restricts to half the base types with a quadratic saving in errors
changed.statement:
∀ (n b q : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 0 < b →
  ∀ (rowCap colCap : Fin q → ℕ),
  let fits := fun (s : ℕ) (G : Fin s → Fin s → Bool) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin s)) (E : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (rf cf : Fin s → Bool) (R C : Fin q → Finset (Fin s))
      (out : Finset (Fin s) → (Fin q → Bool) → Bool),
      (∀ t, (R t).card ≤ rowCap t ∧ (C t).card ≤ colCap t) ∧
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s × Fin s)).filter (fun z =>
        out {z.1,z.2} (fun t => decide (z.1 ∈ R t ∨ π z.2 ∈ C t)) ≠
          Bool.xor (G z.1 (π z.2)) (Bool.xor (rf z.1) (cf (π z.2))))).card ≤ E
  let typ := fun label : Fin (n*b) => (⟨label.val % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ : Fin n)
  let h := (n+1)/2
  ∀ (G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n*b))) (E : ℕ),
    fits (n*b) (fun x y => G (typ x) (typ y)) π E →
    ∃ row col : Fin h ↪ Fin n,
      fits h (fun x y => G (row x) (col y)) (Equiv.refl _) (4*E/b^2)
changed.unlocks: A lower bound on every half-sized matched subtable now transfers to all copy counts with a constant error-density loss.
changed.context: Sample one physical matched name uniformly and independently at each row type. In any column type the hit probabilities from the rows sum to one, so its miss probability is at most exp(-1)<3/8. The expected distinct column count exceeds 5n/8. With probability at least 1/4 it reaches ceil(n/2). Retain one representative per chosen type. Restrict pins and flips and correct singleton diagonals. An erroneous off-diagonal cell is retained with probability at most 1/b² before conditioning. Average on the good event.

changed.title: Sharp peak query degree at minimum depth for recovering block products with arbitrary block-local polynomial leaves
changed.statement:
∀ (a r : Nat), 0 < a → a ≤ r →
  let m := 2^a-1
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let deg := fun (b : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ b) ∧
      ∀ input, f input = (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, input j = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let B := Fin r → Bool
  let low := fun (q : B → Bool) => ∃ terms : Finset (Finset (Fin r)),
    (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card < r) ∧ ∀ z, q z =
      (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, z j = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let run := fun (seen : Nat → Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (x : W) =>
    (List.range a).foldl (fun h pos =>
      h + ((ask pos (h % 2^(seen pos)) x).toNat <<< pos)) 0
  let exact := fun (seen : Nat → Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool)
    (leaf : Nat → Fin m → B → Bool) =>
    (∀ hist i, low (leaf hist i)) ∧ ∀ word i,
      leaf (run seen ask word) i (fun v => word (i,v)) = decide (∀ j : Fin r, word (i,j) = true)
  (∀ (seen : Nat → Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (leaf : Nat → Fin m → B → Bool),
    (∀ u : Fin a, seen u.val ≤ u.val) → exact seen ask leaf →
    ∀ (u : Fin a) (past : Fin (2^(seen u.val))) (b : Nat),
      deg b (ask u.val past.val) → 2^(a-1-seen u.val) ≤ b) ∧
  ∃ (choose : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (predict : Nat → Fin m → B → Bool),
    exact id choose predict ∧ ∀ (u : Fin a) (path : Nat),
      deg ((u.val+1)*2^(a-1-u.val)) (choose u.val path)

changed.context: Each local predictor misses a symbol by full degree of the block product. Choose one forbidden symbol per leaf and block. These form a covering menu indexed by the 2^a transcripts. The menu restriction forces each transcript. In a fixed k-bit prefix, force one zero-side leaf and switch only the 2^(a-k-1) labels on the one side of the tested bit. That query restricts to OR. For the upper bound find a missing a-bit prefix, pad it to r bits, and add its point indicator to each product. The degree-r terms cancel.

changed.title: The two highest simultaneous hit counts for lists of block-local predictors of Boolean products
changed.statement:
∀ (r m L : Nat), 2 ≤ r → 2 ≤ L → L ≤ 2^r → L ≤ m →
  let q := 2^r
  let S := Fin r → Bool
  let Menu := Fin m → Fin L → S → Bool
  let target := fun (s : S) => decide (∀ j, s j = true)
  let low := fun (f : S → Bool) => ∃ T : Finset (Finset (Fin r)),
    (∀ mon ∈ T, mon.card < r) ∧ ∀ input,
      f input = (((T.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, input j = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let legal := fun (p : Menu) => ∀ i a, low (p i a)
  let hit := fun (p : Menu) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → S)).filter (fun word =>
      ∃ a, ∀ i, p i a (word i) = target (word i))).card
  let occ := fun (alphabet labels width : Nat) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin width → Fin alphabet)).filter (fun w =>
      ∀ k : Fin labels, ∃ j, (w j).val = k.val)).card
  let best := q^m - occ q L m
  let collide := occ (q-2) (L-2) (m-1)
  let enlarge := 2 * occ (q-1) (L-1) (m-1)
  let gap := if L+2 ≤ q then min collide enlarge else collide
  (∀ p : Menu, legal p → hit p ≤ best ∧
    (hit p = best ↔ ∃ bad : Fin m → Fin L → S,
      (∀ i, Function.Injective (bad i)) ∧
      ∀ i a word, (p i a word ≠ target word ↔ word = bad i a))) ∧
  (∃ p : Menu, legal p ∧ hit p = best) ∧ 0 < gap ∧
  (∀ p : Menu, legal p → hit p < best → hit p + gap ≤ best) ∧
  ∃ p : Menu, legal p ∧ hit p + gap = best
changed.unlocks: Identifies the two ways a list of local polynomial predictions can first lose successful inputs.
changed.context: Each local error set has odd size. Conversely every odd set is realizable by XORing its indicator with the product. If error sets meet, keep their common symbol and shrink all others to singletons. The collision bound applies. Otherwise a nonsingleton has at least three points. Keep three there and one elsewhere. Each extra symbol costs O(q-1,L-1,m-1) inputs where only its label survives all other columns. A single collision or a single disjoint triple of errors attains its respective loss.

changed.title: Disjoint selections from distinct families preserve a prescribed sum of set sizes minus one
changed.statement:
∀ (v n h : Nat), 2^(9*h) ≤ n →
  let V := Fin v
  ∀ fam : Fin n → Finset (Finset V),
    (∀ i, (∀ s ∈ fam i, 2 ≤ s.card) ∧
      (∀ s ∈ fam i, ∀ u ∈ fam i, s ≠ u → Disjoint s u) ∧
      (fam i).sum (fun s => s.card-1) = h) →
    ∃ (I : Finset (Fin n)) (pick : Fin n → Finset V),
      I.card ≤ h ∧ (∀ i ∈ I, pick i ∈ fam i) ∧
      (∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j ∈ I, i ≠ j → Disjoint (pick i) (pick j)) ∧
      (I.biUnion pick).card = I.card + h
changed.unlocks: Produces an exact disjoint selection of weight h from distinct column families for every h.
changed.context: Induct on h. A weight-h set finishes. Otherwise use the split into red and blue with a common gain on sufficiently many families. Since 2h≤2^h, at least 2 times 2^(6h) families survive. Reserve disjoint halves for the two colors. On a side of weight u≤2h/3 induct using 2^(9u) families. For a heavier side choose its one set. The two selections use distinct families and disjoint vertex colors, and their gains add to h.

Since 2h≤2^h, at least 2 times 2^(6h) families survive. Reserve disjoint halves for the two colors. On a side of weight u≤2h/3 induct using 2^(9u) families. For a heavier side choose its one set. The two selections use distinct families and disjoint vertex colors, and their gains add to h.

changed.title: Translation covers on square alphabets have logarithmic excess over the number of coordinates
changed.statement:
∀ (q m : Nat), 2 ≤ q → q ≤ m →
  let W := Fin m → Fin q
  let covers := fun (C : Finset W) => ∀ w : W, ∃ y ∈ C, ∀ i, y i ≠ w i
  let t := m-q+2
  let b := 2^t * (t*(Nat.clog 2 m + 1)+1)
  (∀ (h : Nat) (C : Finset W), 2^(9*h) ≤ m → C.card ≤ m+h →
    ∃ x : W, ∀ y ∈ C, ∃ j, y j = x j) ∧
  (∃ C : Finset W, covers C ∧ C.card ≤ q-2+b) ∧
  (q = m → ∃ C : Finset W, covers C ∧ C.card ≤ q+2*Nat.clog 2 q)
changed.unlocks: Forces logarithmic additive excess in each fixed difference between dimension and alphabet size.
changed.context: Pad to m+h labels. Each column has at least h repeated labels beyond its first representatives. Trim its equal-symbol groups to total gain h. Disjoint selections of gain h strike k+h labels in k columns. Strike the rest separately. Above, adjoin q-2 constants to binary rows whose t-wise projections are full. The union bound on missing patterns works with the stated row count. At m=q use two binary constants and each address bit and its complement, so every pair of columns sees all four patterns.

Disjoint selections of gain h strike k+h labels in k columns. Strike the rest separately. Above, adjoin q-2 constants to binary rows whose t-wise projections are full. The union bound on missing patterns works with the stated row count. At m=q use two binary constants and each address bit and its complement, so every pair of columns sees all four patterns.

changed.title: One two-coloring splits many disjoint set families into two prescribed positive gains
changed.statement:
∀ (v n h : Nat), 0 < n → 2 ≤ h →
  let V := Fin v
  let P := Finset (Finset V)
  let gain := fun (p : P) => p.sum (fun s => s.card-1)
  ∀ fam : Fin n → P,
    (∀ i, (∀ s ∈ fam i, 2 ≤ s.card ∧ s.card-1 < h) ∧
      (∀ s ∈ fam i, ∀ u ∈ fam i, s ≠ u → Disjoint s u) ∧ gain (fam i) = h) →
    ∃ (red : Finset V) (redGain : Nat) (I : Finset (Fin n)),
      0 < redGain ∧ redGain < h ∧ n ≤ I.card * h * 4^h ∧
      ∀ i ∈ I,
        let left := (fam i).filter (fun s => s ⊆ red)
        let right := (fam i).filter (fun u => Disjoint u red)
        fam i = left ∪ right ∧ gain left = redGain ∧ gain right = h-redGain ∧
        (2*h < 3*redGain → left.card = 1) ∧
        (2*h < 3*(h-redGain) → right.card = 1)
changed.unlocks: Finds many columns respecting one two-coloring with the same two gains and singleton heavy sides.
changed.context: In each family isolate a set of weight at least h/3 if one exists, putting a weight above 2h/3 alone. Otherwise take sets until their sum first reaches h/3, staying below 2h/3. Both sides have positive weight. The sets constrain at most 2h vertices. A uniform two-coloring realizes the chosen assignment with probability at least 4^(-h). Count colorings against families, then pigeonhole the red weight among fewer than h choices.

changed.title: Binary column projections count every missed input in a constant-plus-binary translation menu
changed.statement:
∀ (bigCount m k : Nat), bigCount+2 ≤ m →
  let A := Fin (bigCount+2)
  let W := Fin m → A
  let onto := fun (n : Nat) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n → Fin bigCount)).filter (fun word => ∀ symbol, ∃ pos, word pos = symbol)).card
  ∀ rows : Fin k → Fin m → Bool,
    let hit := fun (w : W) =>
      (∃ c : Fin bigCount, ∀ i, (w i).val ≠ c.val+2) ∨
      (∃ j : Fin k, ∀ i, (w i).val ≠ (rows j i).toNat)
    let seen := fun (S : Finset (Fin m)) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).image (fun j => fun i : S => rows j i.val)).card
    let missing := (Finset.univ : Finset W).filter (fun w => ¬ hit w)
    missing.card =
      (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin m))).sum (fun S =>
        (2^S.card - seen S) * onto (m-S.card)) ∧
    (missing = ∅ ↔ ∀ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card = m-bigCount → seen S = 2^S.card)
changed.unlocks: Counts uncovered inputs of the near-square construction and characterizes its exact binary projection requirement.
changed.context: Group inputs by their exact binary-coordinate set S. Missing every constant requires the large part to use all b large symbols. A successful binary row must be the bitwise complement of the input on S. The number of failing binary patterns is therefore 2^|S| minus the projection size. At |S|=m-b the outside can be filled by a permutation of the large symbols. Smaller S extend to this size and larger S cannot contain all large symbols outside.
